Mount name as in your journal. PUI Mount uses the swimmer underwater, the flyer where you can fly and the ground mount elsewhere; left empty, a random favourite. Press Write macros after a change.

Colour the border of uncommon and better items by quality.
Font, size, colour and (in the Phoenix window) position of the stack number.

BoE on bind-on-equip gear and WuE on warbound-until-equipped items, bottom left.

Same switch as Item Level › Bags; size and colour are set there.

Automation's setting, shown here too. Repairing is on the Automation page.

label: Bugs
desc: Catches Lua errors, blocked actions and warnings from every addon, with a viewer to read and copy them.

rows.d: Every addon (like BugSack) or only Phoenix UI's own errors. BugGrabber, if installed, keeps catching everything either way.
Also keep LUA_WARNING messages (deprecated calls, missing files).
Also keep ADDON_ACTION_BLOCKED and ADDON_ACTION_FORBIDDEN – the usual sign of taint.
Older reports are dropped first. Shared by all characters on this account.
Browse, search and copy reports. Also: /pui bugs, the data bar or the minimap indicator.
One line in chat the first time each error appears, with a link to the viewer.
Play a sound on a new error (at most once every 10 seconds).
Pulse the minimap indicator and the data-bar count.
A small bug button on the minimap. Click: viewer, right-click: these settings. Move it with Movers.
Blizzard's own Lua error popup (the scriptErrors setting). Turn it off to stay uninterrupted and read errors here. Blizzard's blocked-action dialog cannot be hidden safely.

rows.l: Send error reports to the author
rows.d: Sends the error text, call stack, local variables, addon and game version and client language to VQ8S.com. Character names, realms, chat and account details are removed first. Needs Phoenix Uploader running; a change reaches it at your next /reload or logout.
Random, created once, no personal data. Quote it when you ask for help with an uploaded report.
Delete every stored report from every session. Reports already uploaded stay on VQ8S.com.

Phoenix's own quest window for every page: the NPC's quest list, offers with all their rewards (real icons in quality frames), what you still need, and turn-in with reward cards to pick from. PvP-flagged offers keep Blizzard's window. Off: Blizzard's quest window, restyled. Applies live.
Blizzard's spot: where the game opens its quest window (the left window slot). Own place: move it in layout mode.

Phoenix's own inspect window: name, level, specialization, guild and average item level, every gear slot as a card (real icon in its quality frame, item level, enchanted and gem marks) around the player's model. Talents and PvP: the arrow opens Blizzard's window. Off: Blizzard's window, restyled. Applies live.
Adds a button beside the mail recipient box that lists your other characters on this realm.
The transmog window: slots, outfit bar and Apply in the Phoenix look.
The housing dashboard: catalogue, plots and neighbourhood in the Phoenix look.
The battleground and arena scoreboard and match results: a dense table with team-coloured rows, your row in the accent and Phoenix buttons.
Every transmog set with how many pieces you own, the closest to complete first, with a search.
The filter dialog of the Premade Groups Filter addon, when it is installed.
Phoenix: a raised title strip and accent title. Minimal: plain title, no strip. Blizzard: the title and portrait stay Blizzard's.
Phoenix: a flat close glyph that lights up in your accent. Blizzard: the red button.
Window tabs as flat panels; the selected one is outlined in your accent.
Shift+drag a Blizzard window (character, spellbook, group finder, mail …) to move it and keep the spot; Ctrl+drag moves it for this session only.
Put every moved Blizzard window back where Blizzard places it.

label: Spell History
desc: A strip of your most recent casts, with failed casts marked.

rows.d: Adds the cast as a grey icon with a red cross.
Seconds before an icon fades. 0 keeps icons until replaced.
Record casts only while in combat.
Position this element in Edit Mode.

label: Tooltip
desc: A cleaner tooltip with class borders and names, health bar, cursor or mover anchoring, inspect, mount, guild rank, targeted-by lines and IDs.

rows.d: Dark background and thin border.
Restyle the unit health bar.
Color the border by the player's class.
Color the border by item quality.
Use your fonts for every tooltip line.
Where tooltips that use the default position appear.
Hide tooltips while in combat. Hold the key below to see them anyway.
Hold this key in combat to see a hidden tooltip.
Which tooltips hide in combat: units only, or every tooltip (spells, items, buttons).
Players' names in their class colour.
NPC names in red, yellow or green by how they see you; grey when someone else tagged them.
Add the player's rank after their guild name.
Show the realm of players from other realms.
Blank out the "PvP" line on flagged units.
Write the unit's health percent on the health bar.
Show what the unit is targeting.
List the group members who have this player targeted.
Show the group role icon.
Inspect players you point at (out of combat, a few at a time) and show their equipped item level and specialization. Results are kept for five minutes.
The mount a player is riding, and whether you own it (out of combat).
How many you have in your bags, bank and warband bank.
Adds what a vendor pays for the item when the game's tooltip shows no sell price.
On a herb, ore or skinnable tooltip that names one of your gathering skills, adds your skill level: green when you can gather it, red when not. Applies live.
On appearances, toys, mounts and pets: a line saying whether you already have it.
On a keystone: the dungeon's timer for its level and your best run there this season.
Score, key level and role lines on group finder listings are set on the Group Finder page.
Show a player's current season rating in Blizzard's rarity color.
A line on items you simmed on the Sim page: the DPS gain or loss and when.
Paste item IDs (or a PUI-BIS: string) and those items get a Best in slot line. Your own list; none ships with Phoenix.
Show IDs at the bottom of tooltips; the cog picks which kinds.

label: Cooldown Manager
desc: Blizzard's Cooldown Manager in Phoenix style and layout, three custom bars for spells, items and trinkets, glows, keybinds, visibility rules and pre-pull reminders.

rows.d: Turn on Blizzard's Cooldown Manager (configure it in Edit Mode).
Opens Blizzard's Cooldown Manager settings, where you pick the spells and auras each viewer shows.
Sample icons and bars where every viewer, custom bar and the reminders sit, to set them up out of a fight.
Drag the viewers placed by Phoenix, the custom bars and the reminders. Viewers on Edit Mode move in Edit Mode.
A Phoenix bar for what the Cooldown Manager cannot show: other spells, items and trinkets.

Spell IDs or names, item:ID, trinket1 / trinket2, separated by commas. Spells you do not know and items you do not carry are skipped. Add ?ID after an entry to show it only with that talent, !ID only without it.
Fill this bar with your class's movement cooldowns (blink, dash, charge …).
Adds both trinket slots when the trinket has a use effect.
Always, only while on cooldown, or only when ready.
Show the charge count and the recharge ring for spells with charges.
Lay the icons out with the settings below instead of Edit Mode's. The viewer itself stays an Edit Mode system.
Make the second and later rows bigger or smaller than the first.
Where the next row goes. It must cross the grow direction.
A row with fewer icons sits in the middle instead of at the start.
Hidden icons keep their slot, so the others never shift.
What happens to icons beyond the rows set above.
Edit Mode keeps the icons on the viewer's Edit Mode spot; Phoenix mover places them anywhere with Layout mode.
Dress this viewer's icons and texts and lay them out on Phoenix's grid. Which spells show stays Blizzard's choice (Choose spells).
Crisp square icons with a Phoenix border instead of Blizzard's rounded ring.
Removes the coloured frame Blizzard draws around tracked debuffs.
A shading gradient over the fill of the tracked bars: darker at the start (horizontal) or at the bottom (vertical).
Icons lose their colour while the spell is on a real cooldown (not the global cooldown).
No swipe for the short global cooldown, only for real ones.
Keep Blizzard's red tint when the target is out of range and the dim look when you lack resources.
Show the key of the action button that holds the spell.
How an icon glows when the game lights up the spell (a proc or an empowered cast).
Glow a cooldown while an aura is on you: spellID=auraID, separated by commas (e.g. 11366=48108).
A glow when a cooldown comes back. Viewers glow briefly; custom bars glow while the spell is ready.
Cooldown Text styles them like every other cooldown (one setting for all); or this viewer claims them with its own timer font.
Icons for what is missing before a pull, out of combat only.
Stay quiet in the open world.
When you can cast a raid buff (Arcane Intellect, Fortitude …) and it is missing on you.
When a warlock is in your group (or you are one) and you carry none.
Warns for a few seconds when a ready check starts and your mana is below the threshold.
When this viewer or bar is visible. Out-of-combat fading applies on top.
A whole different Cooldown Manager setup per specialization: pick a profile for each spec on the Profiles page.
Viewers and custom bars dim to the chosen opacity when you are not fighting and come back the moment combat starts.

label: Unit Frames
desc: Textures, colors and fonts for player, target, focus and pet frames.

rows.d: Phoenix frames replace Blizzard's player, target, focus, pet and boss frames. Blizzard keeps the game's frames and only reskins them. Changing this reloads the interface.
Sample frames for every unit in your style, where the real ones sit. Press again to hide; they also hide when combat starts.
Opens Layout mode, where every Phoenix frame has a mover you can drag and snap.
Use the bar texture from General.
Color player health bars by class.
Color power bars by resource type.
Target, focus and pet fade when they are group members more than 40 yards away. The game does not tell addons the range of enemies, so enemy frames stay solid.
Crops the buff and debuff icons under the target, focus and boss frames, with an optional border and the Phoenix stack font. Their size and order stay Blizzard's.
Turns this Phoenix frame on or off. Blizzard's frame stays hidden while Phoenix frames are in use.
Space between boss or arena frames.
A starting look for the arena frames: it sets their size, power bar, portrait, mirroring and icon crop. Fine-tune afterwards.
Class icon, trinket and racial on the right, auras and diminishing returns on the left.
How many arena frames Test mode and the preview show (2v2, 3v3 or 5v5).
Each arena pet sits next to its owner's frame. Off: the pets keep their own stack and mover.
A texture behind the whole frame, under its health bar.
The frame brightens while the mouse is over it.
A bright border on boss and arena frames for the unit you have targeted.
Phoenix frames are secure unit buttons, so the game's own Click Casting bindings (and Clique) work on them. Opens the game's Click Casting window.
A slim strip under the frame with its own tag text, for example level and class or spec.
Holding this key while left-clicking any Phoenix unit frame sets it as your focus.
Also puts this raid marker on the unit you quick-focus.
Show a nickname instead of a name, for example: Thrall=Go'el, Jaina=Jaina. Separate entries with commas.
Group members more than 40 yards away fade. The game does not tell addons the range of enemies in combat, so enemy frames stay solid then.
Arena foes you cannot see (stealthed or out of sight) fade to this opacity.
The frame fades when you are out of combat with nothing targeted and full health; it comes back when any of that changes or you point at it.
Class colour for players, reaction colour for NPCs, a colour by health left, one fixed colour, or the theme surface.
The health part is dark and the missing part shows the colour, so damage taken stands out.
A soft top-to-bottom shade on the bar. Zero is flat.
The bar slides to new values instead of jumping.
The bar empties towards the right instead of the left.
How much of the frame's height the health bar takes when the power bar sits inside.
Shows absorb shields on the health bar, after the current health.
Effects that soak up healing show as a dark part at the end of the health.
Heals being cast on the unit show ahead of its health.
How far incoming heals may draw past the end of a full health bar, as a share of its width. 0 keeps them inside the bar. Left-to-right bars only.
Used when the health colour is “By health left”: the bar blends from low to full.
The glow on an arena class icon for crowd control, big defensives and important buffs, and the focus mark.
The bar colour used by the “Theme” health colour.
0 matches the frame. A narrower power bar below the frame is centred under it.
Which way the power bar fills: to the right, to the left, or out from the centre.
The bar slides to new values instead of jumping.
The extra bar some encounters and quests add (alternate power), under the frame.
While you cast, the part of your power bar the spell will spend is highlighted at the end of the fill.
Combo points, holy power, soul shards, chi, arcane charges, essence, runes and stagger on the player frame, or on their own mover.
Ready runes first, then by time left.
Brewmaster monks see stagger as a bar coloured green, yellow or red by how heavy it is.
Hides the class resource out of combat while it sits at its resting value (full runes, no combo points).
Thin lines between the pips of a bar-shaped class resource.
From this many points the filled pips change to the highlight colour (0: off), for example 5 combo points.
Out of combat with nothing to spend, the class resource fades out.
The colour of combo points that are charged.
Text with tags in square brackets, for example [name] or [health:current-percent]. Leave empty to hide.
Text with tags in square brackets, for example [name] or [health:current-percent]. Leave empty to hide.
Text with tags in square brackets, for example [name] or [health:current-percent]. Leave empty to hide.
Text with tags in square brackets, for example [name] or [health:current-percent]. Leave empty to hide.
Use the unit font for names and values.
Names longer than this many letters are cut short.
The health text fades out while the unit is at full health.
How health and power numbers are written.
A flat face picture, a live 3D model, the class icon for players, or no portrait.
The game's 3D-rendered face, the class icon for players, or no portrait.
The side portrait's size against the frame height, centred on the frame.
A ring in the unit's class colour around a round portrait.
The game's gold dragon or silver star around the portrait of elites, bosses and rares.
A small star for elite, rare and boss units.
The frame edge glows yellow, orange or red as the unit's threat on you rises.
Shows ready, not ready or waiting during a ready check.
Debuff borders take the colour of their type: magic, curse, disease, poison, enrage or bleed.
On enemy frames, debuffs you did not cast are shown in grey.
Pointing at an aura icon shows its tooltip. Off lets clicks pass through to the frame.
Where the frame's cast bar sits. Until Phoenix cast bars arrive, Blizzard's own target, focus and boss cast bar is placed here.
Shows each arena foe's PvP trinket and its cooldown.
Shows each arena foe's specialization.
Each arena foe's racial ability beside the trinket, with its cooldown once it is used.
A square class icon at the frame's side, with the spec badge on its corner.
Crowd control, big defensives and important buffs replace the class icon while they last, with their time.
The game's own diminishing-returns tracker for each arena foe, restyled and placed beside the Phoenix frame.
A red edge on a category once the foe is immune to it.
Hide categories your character cannot cause (the game's own option).
Marks the enemy healer even when role icons are off.
A small mark on the arena frame of your focus.
Pips in class colours for each of you and your party targeting that foe.
Your health, power, class resource and spec bar as one movable block near the centre of the screen.
Which class the preview shows; the bars in game always follow your character.
Rows your class or spec does not use take no space.
Out of combat the block uses the opacity set in the cog.
Combo points, holy power, chi, soul shards, runes, essence and the like, with the Power tab's class resource look.
A bar for your spec's key buff: Ironfur, Ignore Pain, Sweeping Strikes, Soul Fragments or Ebon Might.
Blizzard's totem frame, Phoenix buttons (movable, right-click destroys), or none.
An icon for each weapon with a temporary enchant (poison, oil, stone, shaman weapon spell): the weapon's own icon, the time left and its charges. Movable in Layout mode. Applies live.
